name: Medium Brown
lede: Medium Brown is exactly what it says: a mid-depth [[brown]], placed between the lighter and darker members of the family by the online xkcd color survey.

sections.title: A plain modifier on brown
sections.body:
The name follows ordinary modifier grammar, "medium" plus the parent hue [[brown]], rather than naming a dye, place or person [1]. It comes from the xkcd color survey, a large 2010 crowd-sourced naming experiment where volunteers typed free-text names for colors on screen [1]. Paterson's dictionary never defines "medium brown" as a term of art; it only notes, in passing, that the pigment Vandyke brown (named for the Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck) can itself be a deep brown or a medium one depending on the batch [2].

Medium Brown's nearest named neighbor by measured color is [[milk-chocolate]], almost the same hue, with [[bismarck-brown]] and [[brussels-brown]] a little further off [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in 1,695 of 23,781 paintings, 7.13 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 906 [3]. That makes it more common than 89 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1300s, found in 16 of the 251 paintings we have from that century, 2.0 times the expected rate [3]. Adriaen van Ostade is its most devoted painter, present in 11 of his 39 works here, well above the baseline for the museums those works come from [3]. Paintings carrying Medium Brown are more likely than chance to also carry Caramel and Dark Goldenrod [3].

questions.q: Where does the name Medium Brown come from?
True or false: Paterson's dictionary defines "medium brown" as a specific named pigment.

openers: Medium Brown comes from a 2010 crowd-sourced color-naming survey, not a dye or a painter.
